paper.core_task: Evaluating motion utilization in video MLLMs for referring video segmentation

contributions.name: A motion-centric probing and evaluation technique
contributions.author_claim_text: we create a motion-centric probing and evaluation technique that questions previous efforts on motion referring expressions segmentation and can be used to drive better understanding of video MLLMs performance.
contributions.description: A method to create a benchmark by pairing a dynamic video with a static keyframe that approximates the motion expression, designed to mislead models into believing motion is present when it is not.

contributions.name: Strong static-biased baselines for referring video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: We establish strong single-image and semi-temporal baselines for referring video segmentation using powerful multi-modal large language models that can visually ground objects on the region level.
contributions.description: Three baselines built on multi-modal large language models (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL) and SAM that rely primarily on static information from a single keyframe, which nevertheless outperform state-of-the-art methods.

contributions.name: Analysis of motion referring expression properties
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose quantitative means to analyze the properties existing in referring expressions that can drive better evaluation for the use of motion beyond a single image.
contributions.description: An analysis that groups motion referring expressions into dynamic and static categories based on false positives in the keyframe, identifying properties like multi-step actions and dynamic verb phrases that differentiate them.

novelty_claims.text: The proposed method is not novel. The proposed method is just a simple baseline that uses the static keyframe for segmentation.
